_what_this_is: The vectors both implementations of the fallback-disclosure rule read. domain/accounting/payment_account.row_notice is the authority; apps/web/lib/accounting/postingAccountNotice.ts is the keystroke mirror, needed because the client Sales tab reads `receipts` straight over PostgREST and never sees the API's stamped answer.
_why_a_mirror_at_all: The rule is a two-column predicate, not a computation, and the alternative is moving a working screen onto the API purely to render one sentence. The repository already takes this trade for GSTIN, UQC, invoice numbers and GST line tax: one authority, one mirror, one fixture both suites read.
notice: No bank account was recorded on this document, so it posted to the firm's general Bank ledger. Set the account to attribute it.

cases.why: the common case — nothing named an account and the mode moves money through one
a cheque is a BANK mode
no mode recorded either — still not attributable
a stated account wins whatever the mode says
cash goes to Cash in Hand, which is a decision and not a fallback
SPACE, the spelling a human types — a first version of the resolver normalised the hyphen on the input and the space on the constant, so this matched neither and was treated as a bank payment
an EMPTY account id is not an account — the column is nullable and a blank string reaches it from a form that cleared the picker

_two_cases_this_rule_deliberately_cannot: A bank account that IS recorded but has no ledger of its own (`coa_account_id` null). It falls back, and the CA is told in the POSTING CONFIRMATION, where the resolver's own answer is to hand.
A cash payment at a client whose chart of accounts has no Cash in Hand ledger. Same: posting-time only.

Both are facts about the chart of accounts at the moment of posting, and seeing them from a list row would need a lookup PER ROW — the read-proportional-to-the-ledger shape CLAUDE.md forbids in a report. A silent row is not a claim that the posting was attributable.
